newsitem.title: FRANCE: Strauss-Kahn says achievement of EMU not in doubt.
newsitem.headline: Strauss-Kahn says achievement of EMU not in doubt.

text.p: The French government's views on interpretation of the Maastricht treaty on monetary union do not cast doubt on achievement of a single currency, Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said on Tuesday.
Monetary policy cannot be used to help economic growth but might be used after introduction of the euro, he added at a Paris Europlace conference.
"The fact that the government has precise ideas about how the Maastricht Treaty should be put in place, in all its aspects, doesn't mean that there should be doubts about monetary union," he said.
"On the contrary it shows a willingness to launch a single currency under the best conditions," Strauss-Kahn said. "Some wanted to see a contradiction where there were complementary elements."
He said France was totally committed to ensuring price stability in the euro zone and ensuring the independence of a future European central bank.
"Budget stability, price stability, central bank independence...the government is totally committed to these three elements," Strauss-Kahn said.
"Monetary policy is not an instrument for fueling growth in the way the United States did...Maybe when the euro has been launched we could consider it," Strauss-Kahn said.
